entries.issuing_body: New York State Department of Financial Services
entries.title: NYDFS issues advertising and marketing guidance for all New York licensed and chartered virtual currency entities
entries.facts: A NYDFS press release dated November 12, 2026 states that Acting Superintendent Kaitlin Asrow issued guidance on policies and procedures for advertising and marketing materials covering virtual currency products, services and activities, and that the guidance applies to virtual currency entities licensed or chartered by the Department. The accompanying industry letter, headed "Industry Letter - November 12, 2026: Guidance on Advertising and Marketing", is addressed to all virtual currency business entities licensed under 23 NYCRR Part 200 or chartered as limited purpose trust companies under the New York Banking Law. The letter states that VCEs must develop, maintain and enforce comprehensive policies and procedures on advertising and marketing, that those policies must on an annual basis be reviewed and approved by the entity's board of directors or a designated board subcommittee, that materials must not directly or by implication make any false, misleading or deceptive representations or omissions, and that disclosures must in all cases be clear and conspicuous. On timing the two documents differ: the industry letter states that effective May 12, 2027 policies and procedures consistent with the guidance must be available for Departmental review, while the press release states that entities are expected to update their policies by May 10, 2027. The industry letter is published at https://www.dfs.ny.gov/industry-guidance/industry-letters/il20261110-guidance-on-advertising-and-marketing and carries no industry letter number.
entries.relevant_to: BitLicensees, limited purpose trust companies, crypto exchanges and wallet providers marketing into New York, and their marketing and compliance teams

entries.title: CFTC and the United States sue Arkansas and its Attorney General in federal court over prediction-market jurisdiction
entries.facts: CFTC Release Number 9325-26, dated November 13, 2026 and titled "CFTC Files Lawsuit Against Arkansas as the Agency Defends its Federal Jurisdiction Over Prediction Markets", states that the agency filed a lawsuit against Arkansas to block the state's attempts to halt event-contract trading, and that Arkansas is the 11th state the CFTC has sued. Chairman Michael S. Selig is quoted in the release saying that the CFTC will continue to defend its sole jurisdiction over these federally regulated markets as granted by Congress under the Commodity Exchange Act. The complaint, retrieved from the court record, is captioned in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Arkansas, Central Division, brought by the United States of America and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission against the State of Arkansas and Tim Griffin in his official capacity as Attorney General of Arkansas, and is titled "Complaint for Injunctive and Declaratory Relief". Its page footers show Case 4:26-cv-01255-BSM, Document 1, filed 11/12/26, running 34 pages. The portion of the complaint read verbatim cites 7 U.S.C. 2(a)(1)(A), 7 U.S.C. 1a(47)(A), 7 U.S.C. 7a-2(c)(5)(C) and 7 U.S.C. 5(b), together with the Supremacy Clause at U.S. Const. art. VI, cl. 2, and refers to Arkansas Circuit Court case No. 32CV-26-717 in Independence County. The counts and the prayer for relief fall in a portion of the complaint that was not read and are not described here.
entries.relevant_to: prediction-market and event-contract platforms, designated contract markets, exchanges and brokerages offering event contracts, and operators with multi-state exposure

entries.issuing_body: 21st Judicial District Court, Parish of Tangipahoa, Louisiana (reported)
entries.title: Louisiana state court reported to have granted a temporary restraining order directing prediction markets to suspend operations
entries.facts: Two independently bylined trade reports published November 13, 2026 state that the Louisiana Attorney General obtained a temporary restraining order in the suit filed on November 12, 2026 against prediction-market operators. Casino.org, bylined Devin O'Connor and published 2026-11-13 at 15:10 UTC, reports that the Attorney General secured a temporary restraining order from Tangipahoa Parish Judge Jeffrey Johnson directing prediction markets to suspend their business operations, that the judge found the defendants' illegal conduct is immediately and irreparably harming the State, and that Johnson set a hearing on the state's motion for preliminary injunction for November 30 at 9 a.m. That report also states that as of early Friday, November 13, the named platforms remained accessible to users in Louisiana. Troutman Pepper Locke's Regulatory Oversight publication, bylined Stephen C. Piepgrass and Reade Jacob and published 2026-11-13 at 20:07 UTC, separately reports that the Attorney General filed a state-court action on November 12 against approximately 30 affiliated entities, obtained an ex parte temporary restraining order, and that a preliminary injunction hearing is set for November 30. No court order, petition or docket number was retrieved, the two reports differ on the number of defendants, and the Louisiana Attorney General's own newsroom carries no release on the suit or the order.
entries.source_label: Casino.org, Devin O'Connor, November 13, 2026 (coverage; court order not retrieved)
entries.relevant_to: prediction-market and event-contract platforms, sportsbooks, exchanges and brokerages offering event contracts to Louisiana users

entries.title: Federal Reserve Board announces 2027 pricing for Reserve Bank payment services, an estimated 1.4 percent average increase
entries.facts: A Federal Reserve Board press release dated November 12, 2026, released at 1:30 p.m. EST, announces pricing effective January 1, 2027 for the payment services the Federal Reserve Banks provide to banks and credit unions, identified in the release as the clearing of checks, automated clearing house transactions, instant payments, and wholesale payment and settlement services. The release states that by law the Federal Reserve must establish fees to recover the costs, including imputed costs, and that the Federal Reserve expects to recover 101.5 percent of actual and imputed expenses in 2027. It states that overall, price changes for 2027 will result in an estimated 1.4 percent average price increase for established, mature services. On check services the release describes optimizing check processing windows during low-volume periods and increasing the fees that banks and credit unions pay to process checks, and states that these changes do not impact consumers' and businesses' ability to pay with or receive checks. The release states that the entire 2027 fee schedule for all of the Federal Reserve's payment services is published on FRBservices.org, and links a Board memorandum and a Federal Register notice. No dollar figures appear in the release itself.
entries.source_label: Federal Reserve Board press release, November 12, 2026
entries.relevant_to: banks and credit unions using Reserve Bank payment services, ACH and instant-payment originators, and payment processors whose cost base tracks Reserve Bank fees

entries.title: CFTC Chairman Selig devotes a section of public remarks to tokenization, describing it as broader than native crypto assets
entries.facts: In remarks titled "Remarks at Beer Institute Annual Membership Meeting", datelined Washington, DC, November 13, 2026 and delivered by CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig, a section headed "Tokenization" states that tokenization is another area that the CFTC spends a lot of time thinking about. The Chairman states that when most folks in the room hear the word tokenization or blockchain they likely think of crypto assets like bitcoin or ether, but that tokenization is much broader than native crypto assets. He states that real-world assets, such as U.S. Treasurys, are also quickly moving from standard electronic warrant systems to being issued on blockchain networks, and that there has even been experimentation tokenizing agricultural commodities, like cattle, and energy products. He states that going forward he sees ample opportunities for tokenization to provide innovative ways to address warehousing, and that auditable warranting made available through tokenization and blockchain networks could improve efficiency and transparency in warehousing, reducing the overall cost of doing business. He states that the CFTC recognizes that this technological transition is happening quickly, and that the agency cannot stop technological change by looking away from it. The remarks carry the Chairman's standard caveat that the views are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of the Commission. The remarks announce no rulemaking, deadline or Federal Register action on tokenization, and the exact phrase digital asset does not appear in them.
entries.source_label: CFTC Speeches and Testimony, Chairman Michael S. Selig, November 13, 2026
entries.relevant_to: tokenization platforms, real-world-asset issuers, commodity warehousing and warrant operators, and crypto market infrastructure firms
